page: Microsoft Azure F80ams_v7 is a high-density, memory-intensive instance positioned within the compute-optimized and memory-optimized categories. Powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC 9V45 processor clocked at 4.5 GHz, the instance provides 80 dedicated physical cores running at one thread per core across 80 vCPUs. It features 48 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache per core cluster, alongside hardware support for AVX-512 vector instruction sets, including VNNI and BF16. System memory totals 640.0 GB, yielding a high ratio of 8.0 GB of RAM per dedicated core. The instance includes no bundled local storage and zero GPUs, requiring remote network-attached disks for persistent storage operations.

Benchmark results demonstrate top-tier execution across computing, memory throughput, and concurrent transaction operations. The instance achieved a top-tier stress-ng multi-core CPU score of 288363.19 and a PassMark CPU score of 128041.5, supported by hardware-accelerated cryptographic performance reaching 116676.87 on encryption tests. Memory subsystem bandwidth reaches 476.74 GB/sec for large-block reads and 214.02 GB/sec for large-block writes, with cached small-block reads peaking at 14097.63 GB/sec. Data processing capability remains high with multi-threaded bzip3 decompression at 1056.7 GB/sec, Redis SET operations exceeding 202 million operations per second, and static web serving throughput hitting 110.18 GB/sec. For CPU-based language model inference, prompt processing reaches 6047.2 tokens per second on lightweight 135M models and 349.11 tokens per second on 7B models, though large 70B models show average throughput due to the absence of dedicated matrix acceleration hardware.

The qualitative cost profile reflects a large-scale enterprise instance delivering high performance per resource through dedicated non-hyperthreaded physical cores and expansive memory allocation. The primary tradeoff lies in the complete absence of local ephemeral NVMe storage, meaning all disk I/O depends directly on external managed block storage configurations. Given the 8:1 memory-to-core ratio and sustained compute capability, Microsoft Azure F80ams_v7 is designed for memory-resident databases, Redis caching clusters, high-throughput web serving, parallel data compression, and memory-heavy scientific simulations.
description: Microsoft Azure F80ams_v7 is an enterprise-grade virtual machine built on the x86_64 AMD EPYC 9V45 platform, providing 80 dedicated physical cores clocked at up to 4.5 GHz with a 1:1 vCPU-to-core mapping. It delivers 640.0 GB of system memory, matching a dense 8.0 GB per core profile. The hardware configuration contains zero bundled GPUs and no local storage, requiring network-attached storage architectures. Synthetic and operational benchmarks position the instance in the top tier for multi-core computation, data decompression, Redis operations, and memory bandwidth, which exceeds 476 GB/sec on uncached reads. Extended AVX-512 instruction support accelerates vector operations and CPU-based machine learning inference. While lacking onboard disks, the server provides substantial computing and memory density suited for distributed memory caches, enterprise in-memory databases, parallel data crunching, and high-concurrency web services.
